<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\item[1)] The assignement $\rho \mapsto \rho_{G(Q)}$ is a $1$ to $1$ correspondance between quandle representations of $Q$ and group representations of $G(Q)$.
\item[2)] If $h$ is an intertwinning operator between two quandle representations of $Q$ it is an intertwinning operater between the corresponding representations of $G(Q)$.
\item[3)] The assignement $Hom_{Rep(Q)}(\rho,\rho') \to Hom_{Rep(G(Q))}(\rho_{G(Q)},\rho'_{G(Q)})$ in $2)$ is bijective.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{Rep}
\item[1)] The assignement of the previous proposition $\rho \mapsto \rho_{G(Q)}$ and $h\mapsto h$ is a category isomorphism $F$ between $Rep(Q)$ and $Rep(G_Q)$. 
\item[2)] $F$ is an additive functor and a tensor functor.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
Let $Q$ be a non injective finite quandle. 
\item[1)] The quandles $Q$ and $Q_{Conj}$ are not isomorphic.
\item[2)] We have a category isomorphism between $Rep(Q)$ and $Rep(Q_{conj})$. This isomorphism is an isomorphism of addive categories and tensor categories.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The quandle $Q_{Conj}$ is not isomorphic to $Q$ since $\vert Q_{Conj} \vert < \vert Q \vert$, but $G(Q_{Conj})$ and $G(Q)$ are isomophic (\cite{GQ}). Hence, we have an isomorphism of (additive and tensor) categories between $Rep(G(Q))$ and $Rep(G(Q_{Conj}))$. $2)$ follows from proposition \ref{Rep}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
Let $Q$ be a quandle.
\item[1)] $G(Q)$ and $G(Q^*)$ are isomorphic.
\item[2)] $Rep(Q)$ and $Rep(Q^*)$ are isomorphic categories. The isomorphism is an isomorphism of additive and tensor categories.
\item[3)] $Q$ is injective if and only if $Q^*$ is injective.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We prove $1$. Recall that the enveloping groups of $Q$ and $Q*$ are the group :
$$G(Q)=\langle e_x \mid e_{x\triangleright y}=e_xe_ye_x^{-1}\rangle\quad \text{and}\quad  G(Q^*)=\langle f_x \mid f_{x\triangleright^{-1}y}=f_xf_yf_x^{-1}\rangle.$$
The fact that $z=x\triangleright^{-1}y$ means that $y=x\triangleright z$. Hence, we have the relation :
$$f_z=f_xf_{x\triangleright z} f_x^{-1}, $$
in $G(Q^*)$. Writing this relation differently, we get :
$$f_{x\triangleright z}^{-1}=f_x^{-1}f_{z}^{-1}f_x.$$
In $G(Q^*)$. The correspondance $e_x\mapsto f_x^{-1}$ maps the relation $e_{x\triangleright z}=e_xe_ze_x^{-1}$ onto $ f_{x\triangleright z}^{-1}=f_x^{-1}f_{z}^{-1}f_x$. Hence, we have a morphism $\theta : G(Q) \to G(Q^*)$ induced by the correpondance $e_x\mapsto f_x^{-1}$. Since $(Q^*)^*=Q$ we have a morphism $\theta^*:G(Q^*)\to G(Q)$ given by the correspondance $f_x\mapsto e_x^{-1}$. The maps $\theta$ and $\theta^*$ are inverse to each other and hence they are group isomorphism. This proves $1)$. $2)$ follows from $1)$ and proposition\ref{Rep}. To prove $3)$ notice that that the universal maps $\varphi_Q : Q \to G(Q)$ and $\varphi_{Q^*}:Q^*\to G(Q^*)$ satisfy the equation $$\theta \circ \varphi_Q(x)=\varphi_{Q^*}(x)^{-1}.$$ Hence $\varphi_Q$ is injective if and only if $\varphi_{Q^*}$ is.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
Let $A$ be an abelian group and $t$ be a natural number prime to $\vert A\vert$. The Alexander quandle $Al(A,t)$ is the set $A$ equipped with the binary operation
$$x\triangleright y= (1-t)x+t y$$
for $x,y$ in $A$. $Alex(A,t)$ is an injective quandle $($\cite{ak}$)$. The dual of $Al(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z},2)$ is the quandle $Al(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z},3)$. The quandles $Al(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z},2)$ and $Al(\mathbb{Z}/5\mathbb{Z},3)$ are not isomorphic $($\cite{ho}$)$. More generally one can consider $Al(\mathbb{Z}/pZ,t)$ and its dual with $p$ prime and $t^2$ not equal to $1$ modulo $p$.
<!-- end example-1 -->
